knowledge_gaps: Matching is underspecified: recent/older position boundaries, donor selection, transition direction and smoothing, matching tolerances, text preprocessing, and missing-text handling need fixed definitions. Matching only immediate transitions may leave longer-context plausibility unequal.

The replacement donor remains eligible in the fixed recommendation pool despite becoming part of the edited history. Donor-entry indicators reveal this effect but do not separate it from other ranking changes. Add a paired analysis excluding both donors from every condition.

Recent-versus-older contrasts can conflate recency with changing the final item used to compute the prediction. Include separate final-item and anchor-preserving contrasts. Position-preserving replacements also leave content–position interactions unresolved.

Five users per category and five draws provide limited uncertainty estimates. Draws are nested within users; unmatched contrasts can selectively remove difficult histories. Report per-user effects, matching coverage, and sensitivity to matching tolerances.

The proposal does not directly test repeated lexical interests or prefix arrangement. For an ID-only SASRec model, title similarity is an external matching variable; sensitivity to text-matched item substitutions cannot establish lexical shortcut learning.

Originality 5/10 is plausible for an integration contribution. Potential 7/10 remains speculative without evidence that diagnostics guide useful interventions, while difficulty 4/10 may understate sparse matching and exact catalog-ranking costs. A bounded pilot with runtime limits should precede expansion.
